Answer: A
Reason: The lateral chest X-ray (Figure 1b) demonstrates a distinct, curvilinear calcification along the inferior and posterior border of the cardiac silhouette, which is the classic radiographic appearance of a calcified left ventricular aneurysm. This location corresponds to the apex and inferior wall of the left ventricle, distinguishing it from pericardial, valvular, or annular calcifications.
